articles.title: Victorian Psycho review – Maika Monroe has a blast in unsteady horror romp
articles.summary: The It Follows and Longlegs star tears into the role of a murderous governess in this hit-and-miss adaptation of Virginia Feito’s gory novel. It’s not that hard to figure out why a lower-class woman toiling away in Victorian England would be so easily driven to violently murder everyone around her.
body: As Winifred Notty (Maika Monroe) fills the frame in Victorian Psycho, heading to a new job as governess for a rich family, it’s easy to be on her side. Even as her murderous impulses start to rear their head, they’re made somewhat understandable, although Winifred isn’t just a woman reacting to the various injustices of the time – she’s one responding to a demon within her, a darkness she has chosen to embrace rather than resist. Darkness is her friend, a protection against harm, and a way to possess some sort of control in a world that has denied her any of it.

The actor has become known as a bit of a scream queen (an all too easily crowned title these days) ever since she broke out in It Follows, but despite roles in hits such as Longlegs and Watcher, she’s never really been afforded that much to do beyond looking petrified. Maybe that’s why it feels like she has so much more to give and prove here, really tearing into a character that requires her to do the petrifying. It’s not just the malevolent soundscape that makes it seem like there is an evil within her but Monroe’s unearthly contortions, an all-in, all-body performance that avoids slipping into histrionic silliness.
points: The It Follows and Longlegs star tears into the role of a murderous governess in this hit-and-miss adaptation of Virginia Feito’s gory novel.

articles.title: Allen review – what would happen if ET came back for Elliott as an adult? Turns out nothing great
articles.summary: This good-natured if relentlessly unsubtle family film from Netflix and the studio behind Bluey relies on a cute alien with no personality. It’s important for stories about magical formative experiences to make the point that time marches forward.
body: Allen, the first live-action feature from Ludo Studio – the production company behind a little show called Bluey – has a quirky point of difference. Instead of following a child who befriends a cute little alien then grows into a man enriched by the brief relationship, that child becomes a manchild – unable to move on and haunted by the feeling that his best days are behind him. This twist on convention is enough to pique our interest, but not to sustain it: Allen ultimately feels like a facsimile of countless other films, beholden to, rather than liberated from, formula.

Allen begins in a child’s bedroom, crammed with toys and pop culture ephemera from the 90s: Ninja Turtles figures, a HeroQuest board game, a Magic Eye book. Co-directors Daley Pearson and Jeffrey Walker clobber us on the head with the message that this is the 1990s, kicking off what is a relentlessly unsubtle, if pleasantly toned experience.
points: This good-natured if relentlessly unsubtle family film from Netflix and the studio behind Bluey relies on a cute alien with no personality.
It’s important for stories about magical formative experiences to make the point that time marches forward.

articles.title: Tom Holland Says Starring in ‘The Odyssey’ Has Given Him an ‘Ambition to See What Else is Out There For Me’
articles.summary: Tom Holland has starred in two of this year’s biggest-grossing films – “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” and “The Odyssey” – but he says it’s the latter that will impact the next stage of his career.
body: “I’ve been an admirer of Chris since I can remember, and to have the opportunity to work with him and to have his approval, and to sit in his house and watch his movie and to get a pat on the back, for me, just was like the perfect way for me to start whatever it is that I’m doing next,” Holland explained. “He’s given me a level of confidence as an actor that I don’t know if I had before and I’m very grateful that that is something that I can take away from this.”

Holland said that while he has also learned a lot from his fellow actors (which included his wife Zendaya) and crew members, he would be going into his next project “with this sense of achievement and this newfound confidence in what I think I can do” thanks to Nolan’s film. “That is what Chris and Emma do so well, is they really champion their actors,” he said.

The actor, who has played Spider-Man for over a decade, is understood to be in pre-production for a Fred Astaire biopic which will see him return to his dancing roots, given that Holland’s entry into showbiz was via the West End stage production of “Billy Elliot.”

“I’ve been an admirer of Chris since I can remember, and to have the opportunity to work with him and to have his approval, and to sit in his house and watch his movie and to get a pat on the back…
“He’s given me a level of confidence as an actor that I don’t know if I had before and I’m very grateful that that is something that I can take away from this.”

articles.title: ‘I trusted a lot of people, and the wrong people, and I shouldn’t have’: Charlotte Kirk on navigating Hollywood
articles.summary: The British actor took up writing and producing to have control over what she stars in after a scandal involving some of the most powerful men in the film business. After a recent run as an assassin, a serial killer and a gangster, Charlotte Kirk was looking for something a little lighter, and…
body: Kirk, who also produced the film, approached Jamie Adams, director of several low-budget British films, including Black Mountain Poets, intrigued by his regular use of improvisation. They worked out the story together, says Kirk, but made it without a script. All they knew was that “this was a Christmas movie, these two have got a deadline to make these hit songs and maybe there’ll be some kind of romance. And then it became something else, which is even more interesting.”

We’re speaking over Zoom, Kirk at home in London, where she lives with her partner, a property developer who also helps produce some of her films, and their baby son. In recent years, Kirk has created a career largely defined by genre films, regularly with the director Neil Marshall (known for Hellboy (2019) and The Descent (2005)). They were engaged for a while, and continue to work together, often as co-writers. Their first film, The Reckoning, was a 17th-century-set horror. That was followed by Alien-esque The Lair and erotic thriller Compulsion.

articles.title: ‘Ghost Soldier’ Review: Jim Caviezel Is a Superheroic Soldier in an Uninspired, Retrograde Actioner
articles.summary: If “Walk Hard” was the parody that made it harder to take seriously subsequent music biopics, “MacGruber” did the same for a certain subset of action movies. Directed by William Eubank (“Underwater”), “Ghost Soldier” stacks up one-man-army cliches as early as the opening credits and continues as if…
body: William Eubank's patriotic exercise casts the 'Sound of Freedom' star as a former Special Forces man defending his small Wyoming town from foreign corporate overlords.

Jim Caviezel, who’s increasingly made himself a Hollywood representative for politically conservative ideologies with projects like “Infidel” and “Sound of Freedom” (not to mention a series of faith-based projects that began with “The Passion of the Christ”), does little to dispel that association as this film’s tireless, technologically advanced and morally upright title character. But Eubank’s glossy direction, paired with a merciless urgency (and complete lack of originality) in Chris Papsadero’s script, renders the story’s ripped-from-the-headlines details with too little dimensionality even for it to deliver the satisfaction of a good, bloody B-movie.

articles.title: Palme d’Or Winner ‘Fjord’ to Open 26th European Film Festival Malaysia, Astro First to Stream Selected Titles
articles.summary: Cristian Mungiu’s Palme d’Or winner “Fjord” will open the 26th European Film Festival Malaysia (EUFF) on Nov. 26 at TGV Pavilion Kuala Lumpur. This year, for the first time, some of the festival’s films will also go to home audiences through Malaysian media and entertainment group Astro.
body: Astro, one of this year’s official partners, will release a selection of the 20 titles on Astro First, its premium home cinema service, from January 2027. The titles going to the service have not been named yet.

“Audiences today are more discerning, with interests that go beyond familiar genres, languages and cultures,” said Henry Tan, group CEO of Astro. He added that the Astro First release would “bring these films beyond the cinema and into homes across Malaysia, reaching audiences who may not otherwise have the opportunity to experience them.”

In “Fjord,” Sebastian Stan and Renate Reinsve lead the cast as members of a devout Romanian family. After the family moves to Norway, the way they bring up their children comes under scrutiny. It is Mungiu’s second Palme d’Or. Reinsve can also be seen in Joachim Trier’s “Sentimental Value,” which took the Grand Prix at Cannes in 2025 and won the Academy Award for best international feature this year.

articles.title: Lei Lei’s Hybrid Doc ‘Vertigo Garden,’ About a Botanist’s AI-Replicated Memories, Lands at Asian Shadows Ahead of IDFA Bow (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Boutique sales company Asian Shadows has acquired “Vertigo Garden,” the new feature from Chinese filmmaker and animation artist Lei Lei, ahead of its world premiere in the Envision Competition at the International Documentary Film Festival Amsterdam (IDFA). This is Lei’s second feature.
body: “Vertigo Garden” unfolds at the Lushan Botanical Garden and follows the life of its botanist. His body is found in the snow and ice at the top of Lushan Mountain, with both body and brain intact. Scientists study the brain, use AI to reproduce his memories and set them loose in a digital world. Through conversation, the film pieces together the botanist’s storied bond with the metasequoia tree and his efforts to communicate with the planet’s memories through these ancient trees.
Lei uses the metasequoia to probe how memory, life and the planet connect, combining documentary, 3D animation and experimental techniques.

“I believe that Asian Shadows and its team truly love the film. They will treat this film like their own child and promote it to meet audiences around the world, which for me goes beyond what is called a business partnership,” Lei said.
Lei wrote and produced the film with Chai Mi. It is produced by See-Ray Studio Production, the animation and visual art company Lei founded.

articles.title: Media industry could be forced to improve safeguards after Walliams allegations
articles.summary: Culture Secretary Lisa Nandy could force participation in an industry watchdog to protect whistleblowers, the BBC understands.
body: The government is prepared to force the entertainment industry to improve safeguarding practices unless rapid change is introduced, BBC Newsnight has learned.
Participation in the Creative Industries Independent Standards Authority (CIISA) is currently voluntary.
It comes after an investigation by the Guardian and ITV News alleged that entertainer David Walliams had been accused by several women of sexual misconduct and abusing his position, which he denies.
Nandy said earlier this week that she was summoning leaders from the broadcasting, publishing, film and entertainment industries to "draw a line" in the sand.

articles.title: King Charles appears on Sir Elton John's radio show
articles.summary: The latest episode of Rocket Hour will air on the monarch's 78th birthday on Saturday.
body: King Charles III has appeared on Sir Elton John's radio show in an episode set to coincide with the monarch's 78th birthday.
During the Rocket Hour show, the King said the pop star had become "a national treasure after all these years", to which the singer joked: "I'll be on the Antiques Roadshow."

The pair discussed some of their favourite musical performances, as well as the role music has played in the King's charity, the King's Trust. The show was recorded in secret last month and will air this Saturday.
Sir Elton has long been a supporter of the trust, most recently donating a pair of his rose-tinted glasses to its 50th anniversary auction this year.

articles.title: DJ Tim Westwood denies two more sexual offences
articles.summary: His latest pleas of not guilty mean he now denies a total of 17 charges concerning allegations from 1983 to 2016.
body: Former BBC Radio 1 and Capital Xtra DJ Tim Westwood has denied two more sexual offences during a court hearing.
The 69-year-old pleaded not guilty to indecently assaulting a teenage girl aged 16 or 17 in Hammersmith and Fulham, west London, in 1991 at Southwark Crown Court on Thursday.
At the same hearing, Westwood also denied sexually assaulting an 18-year-old woman in Wandsworth, south London, in May 2004.
Westwood, of Fitzrovia, in London's West End, was charged in October last year with offences against seven women, which he also denies.

articles.title: Veteran actor Irma P Hall, star of The Ladykillers, dies aged 91
articles.summary: Once a Dallas school teacher, Hall became a star in later life with roles in Soul Food and Collateral. Actor Irma P Hall, star of Soul Food and the Coen brothers’ The Ladykillers, has died at the age of 91.
body: Hall died on Tuesday, her family confirmed alongside a statement that described her as “a beloved actress, author, poet, educator and public speaker whose contributions touched countless lives throughout her remarkable career”.

In an acting career that spanned six decades, Hall starred opposite Denzel Washington, Oprah Winfrey, Robin Williams and Tom Hanks, and worked with directors including Michael Mann, the Coen brothers and Jonathan Demme.

Born in Texas in 1935, Hall was raised with a passion for the arts as the daughter of saxophone player Samuel Player. For 27 years she worked as a high school teacher in Houston before pivoting to acting the early 1980s.
“I always believed I could do whatever I wanted,” she said in a 2001 interview. “I never knew there [were things] I wasn’t supposed to be able to do because I was Black or a woman.”
